tokyo-kanto-rides-myogi-mountain-and-kar.speedBand: 50–80 km/h riding core, local limits always win

sections.advice: High point near Uenohara → Food stop near Miura rides best with patience. Coastal roads change character with wind and visitors; keep overtakes boring and take the photo from a proper stop.

Food stop near Miura → Tokyo / Kanto rides return is the logistics leg. Watch junctions, villages and speed changes, then let the roadbook do its job: move you out of the clutter without spending your best attention too early.

sections.photoQuery: Tokyo / Kanto rides return Myogi Mountain and Karuizawa checkpoint 8 Tokyo / Kanto rides
sections.advice: Use Tokyo / Kanto rides return → Photo stop near Mitsukaidō as clean positioning. Keep it tidy, ignore impatient traffic and save the enthusiasm for the good road ahead. The value here is not drama; it is arriving at the riding section with space, fuel and concentration intact.

Photo stop near Mitsukaidō → Scenic stretch near Noda can flow quickly, but only if you keep village limits and junction sightlines sacred. Fast connectors are where rides get untidy when fatigue creeps in.

Scenic stretch near Noda → Near Kokubunji is the reward section in Tokyo. Look through the bends, use legal pull-offs for photos and keep a little margin for tractors, cyclists and damp shade. The best ride here is smooth, not noisy.

safetyMarkers.note: Respect posted limits and assume enforcement near villages, viewpoints and main-road joins.

scenicChapters.title: Seward Highway
scenicChapters.narrative: For 33 km this is Seward Highway, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it — expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Turnagain Pass → Kenai Lake
scenicChapters.narrative: Water arrives beside the road and stays for 95 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go. Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did.

seward-highway.story: A one-way ride of 333 km, Anchorage to Seward - roughly 4 h 36 in the saddle. On the way it passes Beluga Point, Girdwood, Turnagain Pass and Kenai Lake. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.

scenicChapters.narrative: Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast. For 53 km this is Polish Eagles Nests Route, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it.
